chapter: Wes's death and Monk's turning point
title: Lugging an amplified upright against the congas
summary: The upright was drowned out, forcing Monk to carry a big amp and bass.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: I was still fighting this image of trying to play the upright bass. I wasn't that unhappy with it at this point, but I just couldn't get...Here I am complaining again. Because the sound was so strong. When you think about how firm and heavy Wes played, with the congas...and Buddy was a strong player, he still is. It was like there was no way in the world I could... With the congas, and the drums. Billy Hart is such a strong drummer. You had to be that to give Wes what he was calling for. I just got drowned in it.

So now I got me a big amplifier and a big bass, and I'm carrying these two, just so I can cut through with this thing, right? One day I was saying, I was just tired of lugging them and I had to be...The hassle of traveling that way was really hard on me. And I said to Wes once, we were in Pittsburgh, 'Hey, man, it's not the same thing. Every time I change rhythm the sound changes, the least little thing, if I got a crack in my bass of something, or the amplifier, or there's not room on the stage, or there's always some kind of problem. I can't get comfortable. You know, I better give some thought about going back to the electric bass.'
